dhp309:1: _Pamatta_ can also mean “intoxicated” or “infatuated” (as well as “negligent”).
dhp309:3: _Apuññalābha_ (lit. “one gains non-merit”), _na nikāmaseyya_ (lit. “one cannot sleep when one wishes to”)
dhp310:3: The “king” mentioned here may refer literally to governmental punishment for adultery (which has usually been a serious crime throughout most of human history), or it may refer to Yāma, the so-called “king of death” (see MN130), in which case the “punishment” mentioned here is rebirth in hell as a consequence of immoral behavior.
dhp311:1: _Kusa_ is a type of grass known for its razor-sharp edges, capable of piercing skin if mishandled. For clarity it is translated here simply as “blade” rather than as “a blade of Kusa grass” or something similarly verbose.
